html:
The North Yemen Civil War began on 26 September 1962, when army officers overthrew the new imam of the Kingdom of Yemen and proclaimed the Yemen Arab Republic. It lasted until 1970.

The imam escaped to the northern mountains and rallied the tribes. The war became a proxy fight: Nasser's Egypt sent tens of thousands of troops to back the republic, while Saudi Arabia armed the royalists. Egypt used poison gas, and its losses were later called its Vietnam.

Egypt pulled out after its defeat in the Six-Day War of 1967. In 1970 Saudi Arabia recognised the republic in a compromise that brought some royalists into the government. The Zaydi imamate was over.
sum: The North Yemen Civil War began on 26 September 1962, when army officers overthrew the new imam of the Kingdom of Yemen and proclaimed the Yemen Arab Republic. It lasted until 1970.
